current_determination: Bałaban Part II supplies a source-shaped inductive target in terms of localized analytic polymer activities H(Z) with exponential tree-distance decay, followed by polymer exponentiation into the next effective action. The soft RP kernel must therefore be inserted before this activity estimate, not justified afterward by engineering dimension alone. The naive matrix-Fisher weight written with Re Tr(V Q^dagger) is not literally holomorphic on complexified field variables. A holomorphic repair is available by replacing adjoints with reverse-orientation inverses on the complexified group, but the normalized Markov kernel then introduces a local normalization Z(U); constructive use of -log Z(U) requires a uniform zero-free complex tube and Cauchy bounds compatible with Bałaban's analytic domain. This normalization/holomorphy requirement is now the first concrete analytic interface, followed by the need to prove a Lemma-3-type localized H_soft(Z) bound after propagator/random-walk localization.
major_new_results: The operative induction target is a localized activity H(Z) with exponential polymer tree-distance decay; canonical dimension is only preliminary bookkeeping.

The soft-kernel modification must enter the source chain before Bałaban CMP116 Lemma 3 and survive the same Gaussian/product-measure change, weakening-parameter localization, and polymer exponentiation.
The real-group matrix-Fisher expression Re Tr(V Q^dagger) requires a holomorphic complexification before Bałaban-style Cauchy estimates can apply.
A holomorphic complexified potential can be formed from Q_plus(U)=sum w U_gamma and Q_sharp(U)=sum w U_gamma^{-1}, using Tr(V Q_sharp)+Tr(V^{-1}Q_plus).
The resulting normalized kernel creates a new zero-free-normalization/Cauchy-radius obligation for Z(U), which is not discharged by the quadratic matching of YM-R19.
